explanation: Sundiata Keita founded the empire in the 13th century. Griots, West Africa's hereditary storytellers and musicians, have passed the epic down by word of mouth for centuries.

claims.text: The Epic of Sundiata tells of Sundiata Keita, founder of the Mali Empire.
Sundiata Keita did not found the Ghana, Songhai or Benin empires.
Sundiata Keita founded the Mali Empire in the 13th century.
Griots are hereditary West African storytellers, praise singers and musicians, and they have passed the epic down orally.

evidence.restatement: The Epic of Sundiata recounts the life of Sundiata Keita, founder of the Mali Empire.
Ghana was the older empire, Songhai the later one and Benin a forest kingdom in present-day Nigeria; Sundiata founded none of them.
Sundiata founded the Mali Empire around 1235, after his victory over Sumanguru at Kirina, so in the 13th century.

evidence.restatement: Griots (jeli) are hereditary Mande bards, praise singers and musicians who have kept the epic alive in oral performance.
The Epic of Sundiata, told by Mande griots, is the story of Sundiata Keita, founder of the Mali Empire.
The Ghana (Wagadu) Empire, the Songhai Empire and the Benin Empire had different origins and founders; Sundiata founded none of them.
Sundiata defeated Sumanguru at Kirina around 1235 and founded the Mali Empire in the 13th century.
